conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have three children I'm responsible for - Alex, who's 10, Blake, who's 19, and Charlie, who's 2 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have three children: Alex (10), Blake (19), and Charlie (2).

Let me ask some questions to assess eligibility for each of them. I'll start with some general questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now let me ask about each child:

**Do Alex (10), Blake (19), and Charlie (2) all live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex and Blake live with me, but Charlie doesn't live with me - they live elsewhere.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex and Blake live with you, but Charlie lives elsewhere.

Let me ask about Blake first, since they're 19 years old:

**Is Blake (19) currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now, regarding Charlie who is 2 years old and doesn't live with you:

**Are you contributing financially towards Charlie's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation), and if so, how much do you contribute?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not contributing anything financially towards Charlie at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also ask:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for any of these three children - Alex, Blake, or Charlie?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for any of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Has Blake (19) started working 24 hours or more per week, or are they claiming any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't working that much and isn't claiming any benefits in their own right.

## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility

Based on the information you've provided, here's the outcome for each of your children:

### **Alex (10 years old) - ELIGIBLE ✓**
You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Alex is under 16, lives with you in the UK, and no one else is claiming for them.

### **Blake (19 years old) - INELIGIBLE ✗**
You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Blake. While Child Benefit can continue until age 20 if a child is in approved education or training, Blake is not currently in education or training, so they don't meet the exception criteria.

### **Charlie (2 years old) - INELIGIBLE ✗**
You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Charlie. Although Charlie is the right age, they don't live with you and you're not contributing financially towards their upkeep. To claim Child Benefit for a child who lives elsewhere, you need to contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, accommodation, etc.).

---

**You can claim Child Benefit for Alex only.** If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Blake enters approved education or training, or if you start contributing to Charlie's upkeep), your eligibility may change.
